units.title: Expressions and Patterns
units.blurb: Use grouping symbols, write expressions from words, and compare two patterns.

units.title: Place Value and Decimals
units.blurb: See how places relate by tens, use powers of 10, and read, compare and round decimals to thousandths.

units.title: Multiplying and Dividing Whole Numbers
units.blurb: Multiply with the standard algorithm and divide by two-digit numbers.

units.title: Operations with Decimals
units.blurb: Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths, and explain where the decimal point goes.

units.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
units.blurb: Use equivalent fractions to add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators.

units.title: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
units.blurb: Multiply fractions, see multiplying as scaling, and divide with unit fractions.

units.title: Conversions and Line Plots
units.blurb: Convert units within a system and use fraction operations on line plots.

units.title: Volume
units.blurb: Measure volume with unit cubes and use V = l × w × h.

units.title: The Coordinate Plane
units.blurb: Plot points with ordered pairs and graph patterns.

units.title: Classifying Shapes
units.blurb: Sort two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy by their properties.

topics.title: Order of Operations
topics.short: Multiply and divide before adding and subtracting, unless grouping says otherwise.
topics.trouble: Children work strictly left to right, so 2 + 3 × 4 comes out as 20.

topics.title: Parentheses, Brackets and Braces
topics.short: Work from the innermost grouping outward.

topics.title: Writing Expressions from Words
topics.short: "3 times the sum of 8 and 7" is 3 × (8 + 7).
topics.trouble: Children write 3 × 8 + 7, leaving out the parentheses that the words call for.

topics.title: Prime Factorization
topics.short: Write a number as a product of primes with a factor tree.
topics.trouble: Children stop at a composite factor like 4 and call the factor tree finished.

topics.title: Ten Times and One Tenth
topics.short: Each place is ten times the place to its right and one tenth of the place to its left.

topics.title: Powers of 10
topics.trouble: Children read 10³ as 10 × 3 = 30.

topics.title: Multiplying and Dividing by Powers of 10
topics.short: Digits shift one place for each factor of 10.
topics.trouble: Children "add a zero" to a decimal, writing 2.5 × 10 = 2.50.

topics.title: Decimals to Thousandths
topics.short: Read and write decimals in digits, words and expanded form.

topics.title: Comparing Decimals to Thousandths
topics.short: Line up the places and compare from the left.
topics.trouble: Children think 0.125 is greater than 0.5 because 125 is greater than 5.

topics.title: Rounding Decimals
topics.short: Round to the nearest whole, tenth or hundredth.

topics.title: The Standard Multiplication Algorithm
topics.short: Multiply multi-digit numbers with stacked partial products.
topics.trouble: Children leave out the placeholder 0 in the second row, so the tens product is worth one tenth of its value.

topics.title: Dividing by Two-Digit Numbers
topics.short: Estimate each quotient digit, then adjust.
topics.trouble: Children keep a quotient digit that is too small, leaving a "remainder" bigger than the divisor.

topics.title: Adding and Subtracting Decimals
topics.short: Line up the decimal points so tenths add to tenths.
topics.trouble: Children line up the last digits, as with whole numbers, so 3.5 + 1.25 becomes 1.60.

topics.title: Multiplying a Decimal by a Whole Number
topics.short: 4 × 0.3 is 12 tenths, or 1.2.

topics.title: Multiplying Two Decimals
topics.short: Tenths times tenths make hundredths.
topics.trouble: Children line up the decimal points as in addition, so 0.3 × 0.2 comes out as 0.6.

topics.title: Dividing a Decimal by a Whole Number
topics.short: Share the tenths and hundredths just like ones.

topics.title: Dividing by a Decimal
topics.short: Multiply both numbers by 10 or 100 so the divisor is whole.
topics.trouble: Children shift the decimal point in the divisor but not in the dividend.

topics.title: Estimating with Decimals
topics.short: Round first to check where the decimal point belongs.
topics.trouble: Students accept 2.4 × 3.1 = 74.4 because they never compare it with 2 × 3.

topics.title: Decimal Word Problems
topics.short: Solve money and measurement problems with decimals.

topics.title: Finding Common Denominators
topics.short: Rename two fractions so the pieces are the same size.

topics.title: Adding Fractions with Unlike Denominators
topics.short: Rename to like pieces, then add.
topics.trouble: Children add the tops and the bottoms, so 1/2 + 1/3 becomes 2/5, which is less than 1/2.

topics.title: Subtracting Fractions with Unlike Denominators
topics.short: Rename to like pieces, then subtract.

topics.title: Mixed Numbers with Unlike Denominators
topics.short: Rename, regroup if needed, then add or subtract.
topics.trouble: Children subtract the smaller fraction from the larger one, whichever number it belongs to.

topics.title: Fraction Word Problems and Estimates
topics.short: Use 0, 1/2 and 1 to check whether an answer is reasonable.

topics.title: A Fraction Is a Division
topics.short: 3/4 means 3 ÷ 4: three things shared by four.
topics.trouble: Children do not believe a smaller number can be divided by a larger one.

topics.title: Fractions and Decimals
topics.short: 1/4, 25/100 and 0.25 are three names for one number.
topics.trouble: Students write 1/4 as 0.4 or 0.14, reading the digits straight across.

topics.title: Fraction of a Number
topics.short: 2/3 of 12 is 2 groups of 1/3 of 12.

topics.title: Multiplying Fractions
topics.short: Multiply the numerators and the denominators; an area model shows why.
topics.trouble: Children find a common denominator first and keep it, so 1/2 × 1/2 comes out as 1/2.

topics.title: Area with Fraction Side Lengths
topics.short: Tile a rectangle with unit-fraction squares.

topics.title: Multiplying as Scaling
topics.short: Multiplying by less than 1 shrinks; by more than 1 stretches.
topics.trouble: Children believe multiplying always makes a number bigger.

topics.title: Multiplying Mixed Numbers
topics.short: Rename as fractions, or use partial products.
topics.trouble: Children multiply the whole parts and the fraction parts separately, so 2 1/2 × 2 1/2 comes out as 4 1/4.

topics.title: Dividing a Unit Fraction by a Whole Number
topics.short: Sharing 1/3 among 4 people gives each 1/12.

topics.title: Dividing a Whole Number by a Unit Fraction
topics.short: 4 ÷ 1/2 asks how many halves fit in 4.
topics.trouble: Children believe division always makes a number smaller, so they answer 4 ÷ 1/2 = 2.

topics.title: Fraction Division Word Problems
topics.short: Decide whether a story shares a fraction or measures with one.

topics.title: Converting Units in Multistep Problems
topics.short: Change units within a system to solve a problem.

topics.title: Line Plots and Fraction Operations
topics.short: Use a line plot to find totals and fair shares.

topics.title: Volume with Unit Cubes
topics.short: Volume counts the cubes that fill a solid with no gaps.
topics.trouble: Children count only the cubes they can see on the outside.

topics.title: Volume of a Rectangular Prism
topics.short: V = l × w × h counts layers of cubes.
topics.trouble: Children add the three dimensions, or report volume in square units.

topics.title: Volume as Base Area Times Height
topics.short: V = B × h: the area of one layer times the number of layers.

topics.title: Volume of Combined Prisms
topics.short: Split a solid into prisms and add.
topics.trouble: Children count the shared part twice when two prisms are joined.

topics.title: Volume Word Problems
topics.short: Find a missing edge or compare containers using volume.
topics.trouble: Students confuse area with volume and give square units for a box's capacity.

topics.title: Points on the Coordinate Plane
topics.short: Go across by x, then up by y.
topics.trouble: Children swap the coordinates, plotting (2, 5) at (5, 2).

topics.title: Graphing Points in a Problem
topics.short: Plot data and read what each point means.

topics.title: Comparing Two Patterns
topics.short: Build two patterns from rules, pair the terms and graph them.

topics.title: The Family Tree of Shapes
topics.short: Place shapes in categories and subcategories.

topics.title: Properties Pass Down
topics.short: Every property of rectangles is also true for squares.
topics.trouble: Children say a square cannot be a rectangle, or that a rectangle must have two long and two short sides.
